> could grab it all and then plot it.  But this seems overcomplicated for such

>

First, those labels are the names of the arrays/chip effects plotted, i.e.

ces <- getChipEffects(qa);
labels <- getNames(ces);

You can dynamically change the names by using a fullnames translator
function (cf. http://aroma-project.org/howtos/setFullNamesTranslator),
e.g.

fnt <- function(names, ...) {
  # Example appending "-foo" to all names
  names <- sprintf("%s-foo", names);
  names;
}
setFullNamesTranslator(ces, fnt);

Another, more low-level approach is the following.  Internally, those
functions calls bxp() and passes additional arguments to it (via
'...').  So another way is to do:

plotNuse(qa, show.names=FALSE);
stopifnot(length(myLabels) == nbrOfArrays(qa)); # Sanity check
axis(side=1, at=seq(along=myLabels), labels=myLabels, las=2);

/Henrik

I'm not sure what is going on.  It should certainly not get stuck for
14 hours, unless you're running out of RAM and you're swapping like
crazy, but that should not happen if you have, say, at least 1GB of
RAM.  Are you doing this in a fresh R session?

Where it seems to hang has nothing to do with the number of arrays; at
that stage it is only setting up/precalculating/caching annotation

FYI, there is no 'destfile' argument to downloadFile(), cf.
help("downloadFile", package="R.utils").  Instead:

> library("R.utils");
pathname <- downloadFile("http://bcgc.lbl.gov/cdfFiles/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,A20071112,EP/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,coreR3,A20071112,EP.cdf",

[1] "annotationData/chipTypes/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,coreR3,A20071112,EP.cdf"
> print(file.info <http://file.info>(pathname)$size);
[1] 40108891

For anyone else reading this: R.utils::downloadFile() downloads the
atomically, i.e. it either downloads the complete file or nothing at
all.  Thus, there is no risk of getting an incomplete download, which
you may indeed get if you use utils::download.file().  This is done by
first downloading to a temporary file, which is only renamed when the
download is complete.  Just as most modern downloader are doing, e.g.
web browsers.
